news_title: FDA to establish 50 additional district offices, 13 border posts to strengthen enforcement - CitiNewsroom.com
efet_title: FDA to establish 50 additional district offices, 13 border posts to strengthen enforcement - CitiNewsroom.com
efet_body:
The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) is planning to establish about 50 additional district offices and 13 offices at selected border posts as part of efforts to strengthen regulatory enforcement and curb the circulation of unauthorised products.
Chief Executive Officer of the FDA, Professor Kwabena Frimpong-Manso Opuni, announced the expansion plans at the launch of the Authority’s 30th anniversary celebrations.
He said the FDA currently operates regional offices across all 16 regions, with 10 district offices already fully functional.
The Authority is now working to activate about 50 additional district offices to extend its regulatory operations and improve monitoring of products across the country.
“We have a strong national presence through the establishment of regional offices across all the 16 regions of Ghana. So as we speak today, FDA is found in all the 16 regions of Ghana and we have started a drive of moving further down to the districts and as we speak, 10 of the districts are fully functional and we are in the process of activating about 50 additional district offices and then border posts across the country,” he said.
Prof. Opuni said the expansion would complement ongoing efforts to strengthen market surveillance, product safety monitoring, public education, enforcement and consumer engagement.
Meanwhile, the Deputy Chief Executive Officer for Corporate Services at the FDA, Gayheart Mensah, said the Authority had identified 13 border posts where it intends to establish offices to address the entry of unregistered food and pharmaceutical products.
He explained that some unauthorised products find their way into the Ghanaian market through poorly monitored entry points along the country’s borders, making it difficult for regulators to track their movement.
Mr Mensah disclosed that construction work had already begun at four of the selected border posts, with the Authority targeting completion before December 2026.
“Even as we grant this interview, four of these border posts are under construction. The target is to complete them before the end of this year, before December. It is a step that is being taken in order to manage exactly what you spoke about, the import of products across our porous borders, particularly as we get into Christmas,” he said.
He said the planned border offices would strengthen the FDA’s ability to monitor imports and prevent unauthorised food and pharmaceutical products from entering the country.
